title: 3.8.14 Lab: Handle a Malformed JSON String
description: Write a function that parses text and returns a usable fallback instead of letting a bad string stop the program. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the parsing function
steps.instructions: Define a function named readSave that takes one parameter, a string. Inside it, attempt to parse the text with JSON.parse.

steps.title: Guard the parse with try/catch
steps.instructions: Wrap the JSON.parse call in a try block. In the catch block, return a fallback object with a property such as ok set to false, instead of letting the error escape.

steps.title: Test both paths
steps.instructions: Use console.log to call the function twice: once with a valid JSON string and once with garbage. Confirm the first returns a value and the second returns your fallback.

requirements.title: Function defined
requirements.description: Defines a function. Help: 3.8.12 (Parsing Can Fail)
requirements.hint: Define a function called readSave that takes one parameter, the text.

requirements.title: Parse attempted
requirements.description: Calls JSON.parse. Help: 3.8.8 (JSON.parse — Text Back to Object)
requirements.hint: Inside the function, call JSON.parse on the text it was given.

requirements.title: try block present
requirements.description: Uses a try statement. Help: 2.5.4 (try...catch: Attempt and Recover)
requirements.hint: Put the JSON.parse call inside a try block.

requirements.title: catch block present
requirements.description: Uses a catch clause. Help: 2.5.4 (try...catch: Attempt and Recover)
requirements.hint: Add a catch block after the try, and return a fallback object from it.

requirements.title: Both paths logged
requirements.hint: Call the function twice inside console.log: once with valid JSON text and once with garbage.

requirements.title: readSave parses good text and falls back on bad text
requirements.description: readSave('{"a":1}') returns { a: 1 }, and readSave("corrupted!!") returns a fallback object instead of throwing. Help: 3.8.13 (Example: try/catch Around a Parse)
requirements.hint: readSave must return JSON.parse(text) inside try, and return a fallback object from catch. A bad string must not throw.

checks.expr: typeof readSave === 'function' && JSON.stringify(readSave('{"a":1}')) === '{"a":1}' && (() => { try { const r = readSave('corrupted!!'); return r !== null && typeof r === 'object'; } catch (e) { return false; } })()
checks.fail: readSave('{"a":1}') should return { a: 1 }, and readSave("corrupted!!") should return a fallback object without throwing.
